title: A harmonic observable converts drift-invisible symmetric cubic noise into an exact lifetime threshold

statement.quantifiers: Autonomous independent immigration-death environment N, Z>=1 with eta>0, lambda/mu>=1,H>0 and the displayed cubic birth/death rates; D=lambda-mu.
statement.assertion: L ell=(D-H)(z-1)-mu+eta/z for z>=2, while LZ=eta+D z(z-1); some D>H implies finite-mean almost-sure explosion from every state, all D<=H implies nonexplosion/positive recurrence.
assumptions: Actual falling-factorial jump clock, not deterministic monomial drift or bounded-rate-intensity assumption.
Boundary z1 and autonomous environment recurrence/finite mean return cycles.
Uniform starting-z frozen mean explosion bound required for recurrent exposure.

inputs: Specified birth/death coefficients and legal recurrent environment.
outputs: A sharp equality-inclusive explosion/recurrence certificate depending on symmetric noise.
interface.precision: Exact probabilistic theorem source-reported; no intake stochastic or formal replay.
costs: Favorable state, return time and mean lifetime can be enormous; no computable universal witness/time bound.

Coercive environment-count plus harmonic Foster function handles D<=H including equality.
At a favorable frozen state alpha=D/H>1, invariant weights scale j^(alpha-3); upcrossing means are summable in all three alpha regimes.

Every recurrent visit supplies probability at least exp(-2Mq(v))/2 to explode while the environment stays, and finite mean cycles give finite total mean.
obstructions: Rare favorable-state recurrence alone is insufficient without uniform exposure/explosion probability.
No endotactic or equilibrium-preserving compiler premise follows from the lifetime construction.
